source: User-supplied Wave Race 64 USA revision 1 ROM on VENGEANCE
method: Locally decoded ADPCM samples from bank0, selected by sequence0's channel2/channel5 IO0 and IO5 commands. Seventeen standalone mono WAV effects cover53 note selectors, including starter effect15 with its original loop and quarter-rate tuning. Five additional bank4 spray drums preserve the original loops and half-rate tuning; IO1/IO6 select their note/velocity on independent layer1, with pan from the selector table. An additional ice-break cue renders sequence0/channel7 dynamic-call19: five notes across three layers, bank5/instrument7. The original bank-set resolver confirms these physical banks.
tools: Existing REA/Ghidra analysis on EVO X2
mix: Original samples and tuning; approximate7.5ms envelope steps and150ms release,2s note hold for the drum effects. Starter effect15 and the five spray drums extend their source loops through the note hold before release; spray includes all three envelope stages. Variants share rendered base effects with original relative pitch and pan. Velocity is squared as in the original note interpreter. Whole-channel frequency updates both contact/spray layers; Web Audio pitches the offline envelope/tail along with the sample, an explicit approximation. IO0 has priority over retained IO1 at each50ms physical-frame poll; that phase alignment is a browser adaptation. Ice uses offline SoundFont rendering with approximate envelopes/reverb and explicit peak scaling; its audible tail is faded after480ms and its silent tail preserves the194-tick routine plus8-tick poll wait. Its shared channel coalesces repeated hits. Browser bus gain, pitch smoothing, scheduling, stereo placement, resampling and tails are adaptations, not bit-exact N64 RSP output. Original voice scheduling remains unfinished; engine loops have their own asset bank and live owner.
rights: Underlying Wave Race 64 samples remain the property of their respective rights holders; not covered by the website code license.
riderSource: Sixteen channel10 reaction selectors use sequence0 logical bank8, resolved to physical bank7 by its reversed bank set. Original per-selector tuning is baked into standalone mono PCM; source selectors2/3 are identical. The additional bank0 drum1 is the physical rider-water-entry splash. All files have manifest hashes and original envelope/tuning metadata.
riderMix: Original 240-tick reaction note duration at200BPM/48PPQN, with nonlooping samples naturally ending earlier. Approximate7.5ms envelope steps and5ms end fade. Original IO0/IO1 priority shares layer0; IO2 uses layer1, with fixed source pans64/32/96 for solo/P1/P2. Physical-frame poll alignment and bus gain remain browser adaptations. Original channel reverb sends and delayed announcer commentary are not implemented by this playback subset.
dolphinSource: Three additional standalone bank0 drums8/9/10 from the same user-supplied ROM preserve original 0.75 tuning, envelopes and nonlooping samples. The original sequence0/channel5 IO0/IO5 loader and bank-set resolution were verified against the local sequence bytes. All43 effects are covered by manifest hashes.
dolphinMix: Recovered C1268 commands reach the existing channel5 effect poll. Later IO0/IO5 writes replace pending note/velocity, with contact priority over the shared spray layer. Original distance gain and channel pan update current and future voices. Browser poll phase, linear Web Audio channel gain, smoothing and resampling remain explicit playback adaptations. Existing rider-channel stereo presentation remains separate. Contact manifest and sample URLs use content versions to avoid stale returning-player caches.
